why: Tests allowed to be red without failing the run, each with a reason and the date it went on. A test named here that PASSES fails the suite, so an excuse cannot outlive the thing it excuses. Read by scripts/run-suite.mjs. Policy in docs/canonical/14-how-tests-are-run.md.

tests.reason: Its subject was removed. 'Arrange as a tree' is gone from the canvas menu at the owner's request (canon 02 revision 3, and the comment at Canvas.tsx:646 says so), and every assertion here follows from clicking it. Rewriting it around Tidy layout or retiring it is the owner's call, because deleting a test is.

Same removal. It measures the shape each of Sequential, Waterfall, Tree and Web lays the board out in, and all four buttons went from the rail with that section. Its first half, crossings as laid out by the spawn rule, is still live and is worth keeping when this is rewritten.

Two of its three assertions pass: Tidy layout is in the canvas menu and it leaves every wire exactly as it was, which is the promise the file exists for. The third, that the cards actually moved, cannot be read, and the cause is now known rather than open: this file builds its hierarchy from real spawn events, so four of its five cards are kind 'subagent', and drawnOnBoard (packages/shared/src/index.ts:92) excludes those. One .node in the DOM against five rows in the database is the board being right. The test measures the positions of cards the board is not drawing, so it needs a board of ordinary session cards, or an assertion that reads the one card that is drawn. Not a defect in Tidy and not a drawing fault.

The ceiling itself works: cards are counted, a message at the ceiling is accepted, held rather than typed in, and a card on a permission prompt is correctly not counted as working. What fails is the wording the sender is told (it reads as delivered rather than as held at the board ceiling) and the queued message never being typed in once a slot frees. Not investigated far enough to say which half is wrong, the behaviour or the test.
